title: Short‐Term Forecasting of the Human‐Caused Wildland Fire Occurrence Using a Measurement Error Corrected Random Forest Approach
content:
ABSTRACT

A key component for wildfire risk management is predicting when and where fires might happen. We build short-term (1–4 days ahead) fire occurrence prediction models by adapting the random forest algorithm using an errors in variables approach to account for the inherent forecasting error in short-term forecasts of fuel moisture. Error distributions are estimated using local-likelihood since there were found to depend on the forecasted value due to fuel moisture having a finite range. Our proposed method simulates data from the conditional measurement error distribution and subtract it from the observed variable to create the new error-free variable that is used as the predictor in the random forest model. By doing this repeatedly and aggregating the results from each of these models, we obtain error-free predictions. To assess the model performances, we conduct leave-one-out cross validation using several model performance metrics on our historical data set, and compared across different models. Our modified random forest model, using a errors in variable approach, outperforms the naive models which ignore measurement errors and a simple regression calibration approach. Furthermore, simulations reveal that our modified random forest approach more accurately estimates the underlying cutoff (i.e., split location) whereas the naive approach exhibits bias.
